charset="iso-8859-1"

Distance users,

I am about to carry out a series of analyses on bird populations using =
the DISTANCE engine as a stand alone program. Do any of you know how to =
specify a data filter in the input file? I have a data file that =
contains all habitat types, and I would like to perform a separate =
analysis for each habitat using the data filter function.

Using the windows interface I have specified:
Data Selection Line Transect New Field =3D b1
This works well with the windows interface but it does not show in the =
log, which may guide me to the syntax to be used in the input file.

Thanks

Rick Woodburn
British Trust for Ornithology.

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Distance35 engine as a stand alone
parts:
Hi Rick,

Sorry, but you cannot make use of the data selection feature of Distance 3.5
from the analysis engine. This is because data selection is done by the
distance interface, not the anlaysis engine. You'll have to do the data
selection from within the program that generates the data for the analysis
engine (SAS in your case, I believe).

As an aside, please can you you make sure you send plain text messages to the
list in future - your last one included HTML formatting which will look funny
in some mail programs, and appear as an annoying attachment in others.

All the best,

- Len


--
Len Thomas, Co-ordinator
Distance Development Project
Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
Mathematical Institute, University of St Andrews
Scotland KY16 9SS
